summary.prose: Building this Story means adding one brand-new module, src/workflow/review-round/, with no existing code to extend: a types file for the three shared shapes (ReviewKind, RoundDriverHooks, RoundResult) and a driver file for the one function, runReviewRound, that every review round -- whatever round number, whatever review kind -- runs through. The second task adds the full named test suite proving round-number validation, both hooks' call/error behavior, the security-pass opt-out, and that reviewId passes through unchanged for downstream Stories to use.

tasks.title: Add ReviewKind, RoundDriverHooks, RoundResult and the runReviewRound function
tasks.summary: Create the new src/workflow/review-round/ module: types.ts exporting ReviewKind, RoundDriverHooks<F>, RoundResult<F> exactly as the LLD's dataModel section specifies, and driver.ts exporting runReviewRound(reviewId, hooks, round, targets, opts?) per the contract -- round validation (RangeError for non-positive-integer round), hooks.ground called once per round with the full targets, the optional nested hooks.security pass gated by opts.runSecurityPass, rejection propagation from both hooks, and reviewId threaded through unchanged with no re-derivation.
acceptanceChecks: ReviewKind, RoundDriverHooks<F>, RoundResult<F> are exported exactly as the dataModel section specifies, with no extra or missing field
runReviewRound throws a RangeError synchronously for round=0, a negative round, or a non-integer round, before any hook is called
runReviewRound calls hooks.ground(targets, round) exactly once per call, with the complete targets and no prior-findings argument, for both round=1 and round>1
When opts.runSecurityPass is not explicitly false and hooks.security is defined, hooks.security(targets, round) is also called once and its findings are merged into the same RoundResult

A rejecting hooks.ground propagates its rejection and hooks.security is never called for that round; a rejecting hooks.security propagates its rejection rather than returning hooks.ground's findings alone
reviewId is never derived, rewritten or substituted -- it is the same value the caller supplied, available for the caller to thread onward to sc4/sc5 calls

tests.name: a round 1 call invokes hooks.ground once with the complete targets and no prior-findings argument

tests.name: a round 1 call invokes hooks.ground once with the complete targets and no prior-findings argument
a round 2 (Correction-and-Re-review) call invokes hooks.ground through the identical call shape as round 1, differing only in the round number passed
hooks.ground receives the full targets/artifact unmodified -- nothing is stripped or withheld before grounding runs
round 0 is rejected with a RangeError before any hook is called
a negative round is rejected with a RangeError before any hook is called
a non-integer round is rejected with a RangeError before any hook is called
a rejecting hooks.ground propagates its rejection and hooks.security is never called for that round
a rejecting hooks.security propagates its rejection rather than returning hooks.ground's findings alone
an empty ReviewTargets.entries array is passed through to hooks.ground unchanged, with no special-casing
opts omitted defaults runSecurityPass to true -- hooks.security runs when it is supplied
opts.runSecurityPass:false suppresses hooks.security even when it is supplied
hooks.security undefined is a no-op, not a thrown error, when runSecurityPass is true or omitted
a large round number (e.g. 50) runs through the identical code path as round 1, with no round-number-based branching

reviewId never appears in hooks.ground's or hooks.security's own call arguments across round 1 and round 2, and is left available unchanged for the caller to thread on to the sc4/sc5 calls, never substituted for a different value
